synthesis.description: Combine local-loop procedures with envelope drawing/shapes and explicitly separate sample-loop and envelope-loop states; check launch and repeated cycles.
Before restoring pre-roll, preserve state, obtain approval for the whole-composition move, inspect Lock Envelopes, verify selection endpoints and local codec/export availability.
Do not generalize the VST folder and bank UI to all VST3 builds; do not normalize the uncertain AU filename extension without evidence.

gaps_and_unverified_claims.impact: Exact four-chain example zone coordinates are conveyed by a figure, not extracted text. Text supplies eight-step crossfade and exclusive positions; runtime uses a generic overlap/fade procedure instead of guessing endpoints. No essential procedure blocked.
Extraction prints the AU extension as .au preset. Runtime retains preset directory/behavior and instructs inspection of actual files; no guessed normalized extension.

VST discovery and preset-bank instructions use generic VST terminology despite supporting VST2/VST3. Runtime explicitly avoids asserting a VST3 folder or identical program/bank controls for every plug-in.

Assigned chapters do not establish complete edition entitlements, introduction point releases for A/B/Macro features, current architecture requirements, or OS/codec availability for video. Runtime requires local verification; AU macOS-only and AU3 >=11.2 are retained as explicit evidence.
Text notes A/B access through the Live API with Max for Live. Integration/runtime capability mapping is parent-owned and intentionally not invented here; no tool names claimed.

Keyboard-only breakpoint procedures are cross-referenced to chapter 41, outside this assignment. Mouse/numeric/menu workflows are self-contained here; parent must supply any keyboard-accessibility details from that chapter.

Sidechain Mute and Clear All Envelopes wording follow the supplied text, but UI execution is unverified. Runtime gates broad clears, uses unambiguous Clear Envelope UI rather than the chapter-27 shortcut wording, and makes no proof-of-execution claim.
